channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Flávio admite negociação com Vorcaro para produção de filme de Bolsonaro; veja o vídeo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro confirmed he negotiated sponsorship with banker Daniel Vorcaro to complete a film about Jair Bolsonaro, denying any wrongdoing and stating he sought only private funding for a private project. He emphasized that he offered no advantages, did not mediate government-related business, and received no money or personal benefits. The defense comes amid growing pressure to establish a CPI into Banco Master, which he argues is necessary to separate 'the innocent from the criminals'.

item.title: Aneel congela megaleilão de energia e põe em xeque contratos de R$ 515 bi com BTG, J&F e Petrobras
item.description: Aneel has indefinitely postponed the homologation of the government's energy reserve auction, which contracted R$ 515 billion and is under scrutiny by the TCU and courts. The delay affects contracts with BTG, J&F, and Petrobras, creating uncertainty in the power sector.

item.title: Produtora e Mário Frias dizem que Vorcaro não deu dinheiro para filme e contradizem Flávio
item.description: The producer of the film depicting Jair Bolsonaro's political career and Deputy Mário Frias (PL-SP) issued a statement denying that banker Daniel Vorcaro contributed funds to the production, contradicting earlier claims by Deputy Flávio Bolsonaro. The statement asserts that the film's financing came exclusively from unspecified private sources, not Vorcaro.

item.title: Lula anuncia fim do imposto (que ele mesmo criou) sobre as “blusinhas”
item.description: President Lula announced the end of the 20% import tax on international purchases up to $50, popularly known as the 'blusinhas tax', which had been in effect since August 2024 after being approved by Congress and signed by himself. The move aims to reduce costs for consumers buying low-value foreign goods.

item.title: Caiado pede explicações a Flávio, mas diz não ser “oportunista”
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) demanded explanations from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) regarding audio messages sent to banker Daniel Vorcaro, while denying he is being opportunistic. He urged unity within the center-right to defeat President Lula (PT) in the 2026 elections, even as he critiques allies.

item.title: Pagamentos de Vorcaro ao filme de Bolsonaro superam orçamento de Ainda Estou Aqui e O Agente Secreto
item.description: Banker Daniel Vorcaro allegedly transferred R$ 56 million to the film 'Dark Horse', about Jair Bolsonaro's life, at the request of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro—exceeding the budgets of 'Ainda Estou Aqui' (R$ 45 million) and 'O Agente Secreto' (R$ 28 million). The messages, confirmed by Estadão and part of Operation Compliance Zero, reveal negotiations involving Mário Frias and Eduardo Bolsonaro. Flávio denied the funding, calling the allegations lies, despite the evidence.

item.title: Sóstenes sai em defesa de Flávio e fala em “cortina de fumaça” do PT
item.description: PL Chamber leader Sóstenes Cavalcante (RJ) defended Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) following the release of audio recordings related to negotiations for financing a film about former President Jair Bolsonaro, accusing the PT of creating a 'smokescreen' to divert attention from the issue.

item.title: PT pedirá a quebra dos sigilos bancário e telefônico de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The PT, supported by PCdoB and PSOL, intends to request the Federal Police to break the banking and telephone secrecy of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro following Intercept Brasil's revelations about an alleged negotiation of 24 million dollars (134 million reais) with Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, for a film about Jair Bolsonaro. Party leaders accuse the senator of suspicious financial intimacy, indicating possible money laundering, passive corruption, and influence peddling, given that the amount far exceeds budgets of similar Brazilian films. The group will also file a request with the Federal Revenue and seek to open a CPI to investigate the relationship between Flávio Bolsonaro and the banker.

item.title: Existe um ‘humor sombrio’ no eleitorado que afeta também a oposição
item.description: Analysts observe a 'dark mood' among Brazilian voters, characterized by widespread distrust in institutions—especially the judiciary—and the belief that no candidate can break free from a perceived immutable system defined by taxes, bureaucracy, and insecurity. This skepticism, which includes the opposition as part of the 'system,' is fueled by events like Operation Car Wash and Dilma's impeachment, showing elections do not automatically shift deep social currents. A sense of relative stagnation and the loss of a national 'moral compass' are central, with the term 'moral' frequently appearing in qualitative research as a synonym for its absence.

item.title: Direita critica Flávio por negociação com Vorcaro
item.description: Right-wing politicians not aligned with the PL, such as Romeu Zema and Renan Santos from the Partido Missão, criticized Flávio Bolsonaro after leaked audio showed him requesting money from Daniel Vorcaro, a banker involved in the Banco Master scandal, to finance the film 'Dark Horse'. Zema called the act 'imperdonable' and questioned Flávio's credibility, while Santos labeled him a 'thief' and Kataguiri implied Flávio was complicit with Vorcaro. Flávio's allied base, including Nikolas Ferreira, remains silent.

item.title: Produtor de obra sobre Bolsonaro, Mario Frias afirma que Flávio 'não tem qualquer sociedade no filme'
item.description: Mario Frias, federal deputy and former Special Secretary of Culture under Bolsonaro, defended Flávio Bolsonaro after messages between the senator and banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master were disclosed, stating that Flávio has no stake in the film 'Dark Horse' and only granted image rights for his family. Frias described the film as a Hollywood-standard superproduction with 100% private capital and claimed attacks on it are politically and ideologically motivated. Flávio confirmed the contact with Vorcaro as private, denied public funding or Rouanet Law involvement, and reiterated his call for a CPI into Master Bank.

item.title: Ministro Dias Toffoli é eleito integrante efetivo do TSE
item.description: Minister Dias Toffoli was elected as an effective member of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) by the STF Plenary, replacing Minister Cármen Lúcia, who left the position on Tuesday (12). He ceases to be a substitute minister and joins Ministers Nunes Marques and André Mendonça as titular representatives of the STF in the TSE, with Marques and Mendonça having been sworn in as president and vice-president of the Electoral Court on the same day. The STF also elected Minister Flávio Dino as a substitute member of the TSE. Toffoli noted that his election coincides with the 12th anniversary of his first assumption of the TSE presidency, expressing honor in returning to the court that oversees Brazil’s electoral process, from voter registration to the certification of elected officials.

item.title: Veja cinco filmes que custaram cerca de US$ 24 milhões, valor que teria sido negociado entre Flávio e Vorcaro
item.description: Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master allegedly negotiated a $24 million investment in the film 'Dark Horse', about Jair Bolsonaro, with Flávio Bolsonaro, according to The Intercept. Documents show Vorcaro had already invested R$ 62 million between February and May 2025 — 37% more than the budget of 'Still Here'. The sum is exceptionally high for Brazilian cinema, nearing budgets of international films like 'Emilia Pérez' and 'Conclave'.

item.title: Flávio admite pedido de dinheiro a Vorcaro para financiar filme sobre Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) confirmed he approached Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, to seek private financing for the biopic 'Dark Horse' about his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro. He stressed that no public funds were used and that the contact occurred before suspicions arose against Vorcaro. Flávio also advocated for a parliamentary inquiry (CPI) to investigate Banco Master.

item.title: R$ 134 milhões para um filme? A polêmica negociação entre Flávio e Vorcaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for president, demanded that banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master settle delayed payments for the production of the film 'Dark Horse', which portrays Jair Bolsonaro's trajectory. He expressed concern over potential debts to the foreign production team in audio leaked by The Intercept Brasil.

item.title: Frias nega recursos de Vorcaro no filme “Dark Horse”: “Não há um único centavo”
item.description: Federal Deputy Mário Frias (PL) denied on Wednesday that the film 'Dark Horse', which he produced and which portrays the life of Jair Bolsonaro, received any funding from banker Daniel Vorcaro. He stated there is 'not a single cent' from Vorcaro in the project, responding to an audio leak published by The Intercept Brasil involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The statement aims to dispel suspicions of financial influence in a production tied to the former president.

item.title: STF julga validade de lei que institui igualdade salarial entre homens e mulheres
item.description: The STF began reviewing the constitutionality of Law 14.611/2023, which mandates equal pay between men and women, with oral arguments on Wednesday and votes expected Thursday. The law, signed by Lula, imposes a fine of 10 times the salary for discrimination and requires semi-annual salary transparency reports from companies with over 100 employees. The case includes an ADC filed by the CUT and two ADIs by the CNI and Partido Novo.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro admite cobrança a Vorcaro, mas nega crime
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro admitted maintaining nearly a year of contact with banker Daniel Vorcaro to secure R$134 million in private sponsorship for a film about his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, denying any crime or use of public funds. He stated the arrangement was private, involved no improper benefits, and that Vorcaro failed to pay agreed installments, causing delays in the film’s production.

item.title: Produtora de filme sobre Bolsonaro nega ter recebido aporte de Vorcaro, apesar de Flávio confirmar pedido
item.description: Go Up Entertainment denied receiving funds from former banker Daniel Vorcaro for the film 'Dark Horse', which portrays the life of Jair Bolsonaro. Despite the denial, Flávio Bolsonaro confirmed he had requested the financial support from Vorcaro. The information was reported by Folha de S.Paulo on May 13, 2026.

item.title: O filme de R$ 134 milhões: a ligação entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Daniel Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, a senator and presidential pre-candidate, publicly pressed banker Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, over delayed payments for the film 'Dark Horse', which portrays the life of Jair Bolsonaro. The senator expressed concern about outstanding debts to the film’s foreign crew, in audio leaked by The Intercept Brasil. The film has a budget of R$ 134 million.

item.title: Repasse de recursos de Vorcaro a Flávio Bolsonaro reforça pressão por CPI do Banco Master
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) requested and received R$61 million from Banco Master, owned by Daniel Vorcaro — who is imprisoned and under investigation for billion-dollar financial frauds — to finance a biopic of former President Jair Bolsonaro between February and May 2025. The disclosure, supported by messages and audio from September 2025, has prompted calls for a congressional parliamentary inquiry (CPI), drawing criticism from the government coalition and support from the opposition, despite the senator denying any wrongdoing.

item.title: 'Passando de todos os limites', reage Carlos após Zema criticar Flávio por repasse de Vorcaro a filme sobre Bolsonaro
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) criticized Flávio Bolsonaro for requesting money from Daniel Vorcaro to finish a film about Jair Bolsonaro, calling it 'a slap in the face of Brazil'. In response, Carlos Bolsonaro accused Zema of 'going beyond all limits', referencing an old video where Zema ate a banana with peel to mock inflation under Lula. Eduardo Bolsonaro also defended his brother, stating Zema acted without hearing the other side and used a petista narrative to gain publicity.

item.title: Caiado cobra explicações de Flávio sobre suposto financiamento de filme por dono do Banco Master
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) demanded explanations from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-SP) regarding the alleged financing of the film "Dark Horse" by Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, involving R$ 61 million between February and May 2025. Caiado stressed the need for transparency in relations between public officials, companies, and private interests, stating the senator must clarify the allegations. The case sparked political division, with Bolsonaro allies defending Flávio and opponents, including Romeu Zema and Renan Santos, accusing him of hypocrisy.

item.title: Nas redes, políticos repercutem denúncia sobre filme financiado por Vorcaro: 'Lei Rouanet da família Bolsonaro', diz Paulo Teixeira
item.description: Government and opposition politicians reacted on social media to Intercept Brazil's reports alleging R$61 million in payments from banker Daniel Vorcaro to finance the film 'Dark Horse', a biopic about the Bolsonaro family. Deputy Paulo Teixeira (PT) likened the funding to a 'Bolsonaro family Rouanet Law', while Flávio Bolsonaro's allies deny wrongdoing and dispute the figures. The PL party declared unrestricted support for Flávio Bolsonaro as its presidential pre-candidate.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro deixa, sem falar, QG de campanha em que reuniu aliados
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RN), a pre-candidate for president, left the property used as his campaign headquarters without speaking after an emergency meeting with allies. He departed in his car, avoiding any press statements. The move comes amid speculation about his candidacy and internal PL party maneuvers.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro pedia dinheiro dos fundos sujos do 'irmão' Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is accused of soliciting money from so-called 'dirty funds' linked to his 'brother' Vorcaro, within a network of alliances with families tied to militias and violence. Despite these corruption allegations and associations with illegal groups, he maintains around 40% support in polls for the 2026 Brazilian presidential race.

item.title: Análise: mensagens entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Vorcaro deixam aliados perplexos e colocam candidatura em xeque, dizem colunistas
item.description: Leaked messages between Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro reveal pressure for payments to fund a film about Jair Bolsonaro, causing concern among right-wing allies and casting doubt on the viability of his 2026 presidential candidacy. Columnists Gerson Camarotti and Fernando Gabeira argue that the lack of transparency may have prevented a movement to support Tarcísio de Freitas as an alternative. Flávio denies wrongdoing, claiming the funds were private, but Vorcaro’s ties to the state raise conflict-of-interest concerns.

item.title: Jaques Wagner repercute áudios entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Daniel Vorcaro
item.description: Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) criticized leaked audio in which Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) requested R$ 140 million from businessman Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, to finance a film about former president Jair Bolsonaro, suggesting an inappropriate closeness. Wagner rebutted Senator Izalci Lucas (PL-DF), who linked Banco Master to the PT government in Bahia, stating that Bahia’s involvement was limited to the privatization of the Cesta do Povo network, with no connection to the bank’s creation or expansion, which occurred at the federal level under Central Bank President Roberto Campos Neto.

item.title: ‘Tapa na cara da direita brasileira’, diz deputado rompido com Bolsonaro sobre Flávio
item.description: Deputy Otoni de Paula (PSD-RJ) criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for requesting a US$24 million contribution from banker Daniel Vorcaro to finance a film about Jair Bolsonaro’s life, calling it a 'slap in the face of Brazilian right-wing politics'. Otoni, a former Bolsonaro government ally who broke with the movement and was previously indicted by the STF for insulting Justice Alexandre de Moraes, said the requested amount is nearly five times the budget of 'The Secret Agent' and three times that of 'I’m Still Here'.

item.title: Campanha “Título em Dia” alcança mais de 549 milhões de visualizações no Kwai
item.description: The 'Título em Dia' campaign, led by the TSE in partnership with Kwai from April 13 to May 3, reached over 549.5 million views in seven days. It generated 392,529 posts using the hashtag #TituloEmDia and leveraged Kwai’s strategic tools, including a dedicated page, push notifications, promotional banners, and placement in search and trends. The campaign page received 497,385 views, peaking at 147,185 views on April 15.

item.title: Dino pede providências sobre controle de emendas parlamentares
item.description: Minister Flávio Dino has ordered control bodies such as the TSE, TCU, CGU, Senate, and state legislative assemblies to provide information on the monitoring of parliamentary amendments, in response to requests from civil society organizations warning of possible misuse of funds during the electoral period. The TCU has five business days to report on the functioning of the amendments monitoring panel, and the CGU has ten business days to report on its operational capacity to conduct audits. State legislative assemblies have 30 calendar days to submit supporting documents.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro conversou com Vorcaro quando investigações da PF sobre o Master já eram públicas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for presidency, contacted banker Daniel Vorcaro in November 2025 to request funds for the film 'Dark Horse', about his father's life, despite ongoing public investigations by the PF and CVM into fraud at Banco Master. The messages and audio, confirmed authentic by Estadão, show Flávio requesting financial help and admitting it was sponsorship. Vorcaro was arrested the day after the conversation and Master was liquidated two days later, linking the funding request to an active financial fraud scheme.

item.title: A lacuna na versão de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre áudio para Daniel Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro did not explain his relationship with Daniel Vorcaro when stating he sought only private sponsorship for a film about Jair Bolsonaro, without public funds or quid pro quo. The Federal Police has indicated that Vorcaro sought proximity with public figures to shield himself from investigations or gain advantages in his businesses, revealing a broader pattern that Bolsonaro’s version fails to address, leaving a gap in his defense.

item.title: Confira a pauta de julgamentos do TSE desta quinta-feira (14)
item.description: The TSE will rule on Thursday (14) on six cases, including appeals regarding the rejection of campaign accounts for female city council candidates in Santo Antônio do Tauá (PA) in the 2024 elections. One case involves Aline Ruth Miranda Ataíde, whose campaign accounts were rejected by the TRE-PA, with a ruling to repay R$ 1,041.38 to the National Treasury. The session will be broadcast live starting at 10 a.m. via Rádio e TV Justiça and the TSE’s YouTube channel.

item.title: Romeu Zema diz que áudio de Flávio a Vorcaro é “imperdoável”
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) strongly criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) after an audio surfaced in which he asked businessman Daniel Vorcaro for money to fund the film "Dark Horse", about Jair Bolsonaro. Zema called the request "imperdoável" and a "slap in the face of decent Brazilians," stating that lack of credibility undermines the ability to change Brazil. He also noted that despite criticizing Lula and the PT, Flávio Bolsonaro replicates similar practices, disqualifying him as an ethical leader.

item.title: Silveira pede ajuda ao setor privado para baixar preço da gasolina
item.description: Minister Alexandre Silveira urged the private sector to accelerate the pass-through of government fuel subsidies to lower gasoline prices, stating that companies like Vibra, Raízen and Ipiranga must contribute to the national civic effort amid international oil price pressures from the Iran war. The subsidies range from R$0.40 to R$0.45 per liter of gasoline, costing R$1–1.2 billion monthly, with a maximum cap of R$0.89 per liter. For diesel, the government will replace PIS/Cofins tax exemption with a subsidy starting in June, estimated at R$1.7 billion per month.

item.title: Áudio de Flávio a Vorcaro vira meme nas redes sociais
item.description: Leaked audio and messages attributed to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro show him demanding overdue payments of US$24 million from Daniel Vorcaro to fund the film 'Dark Horse', about Jair Bolsonaro. The content went viral as memes on social media, including AI-generated images of Romeu Zema in a Brazilian national team jersey. The case reignites debate over private financing of political films and banker influence in electoral campaigns.

item.title: Flávio nega ter recebido vantagens de Vorcaro e pede CPI do Master
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) denied receiving illicit advantages from banker Daniel Vorcaro, stating that funds received were solely for sponsoring the film 'Dark Horse' about his father, Jair Bolsonaro. He called for the installation of the CPI Master to 'separate the innocent from the criminals' after Intercept reported messages and audio indicating negotiations for US$2 million for the film. PL allies sought to downplay the scandal, framing it as legitimate sponsorship, though the campaign acknowledged the association with Vorcaro is electorally toxic.

item.title: De 'baixíssimo orçamento' a milhões pedidos a Vorcaro: os bastidores do filme sobre Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro admitted requesting R$ 134 million from Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, in November 2025 to finance sponsorship installments for the film 'Dark Horse', which depicts Jair Bolsonaro's 2018 stabbing. The request was made shortly before Vorcaro's arrest in the Banco Master financial fraud scandal. Flávio denies receiving any benefits and insists the film is privately funded, with no public money or Rouanet law involvement.

item.title: Governistas comemoram (com cautela) áudios entre Flávio e Vorcaro
item.description: Government supporters reacted cautiously to an audio in which Senator Flávio Bolsonaro asked businessman Daniel Vorcaro for money to finance a film about his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, interpreting it as a sign of opposition weakness. The episode reignited debate over the direction of the bolsonarist candidacy in 2026, with analysts noting the funding request reveals difficulties in mobilizing independent resources. The audio, reported by O Globo, was welcomed in government circles as an opportunity to undermine the opposition’s narrative of strength.

item.title: Caiado cobra explicações de Flávio sobre financiamento do filme “Dark Horse”
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) demanded that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) explain the financing of the film 'Dark Horse' by banker Daniel Vorcaro, following the release of an audio in which Flávio pressures Vorcaro for payments related to the production. The statement came on Wednesday, the 13th, after a report by The Intercept Brasil. Caiado stressed the need for transparency amid suspicions of irregularities.

item.title: Financiado por Vorcaro, filme sobre Bolsonaro teve set fiscalizado após relatos de atraso em pagamento e comida estragada
item.description: The film 'Dark Horse', about Jair Bolsonaro and financed by Daniel Vorcaro, faced allegations of poor working conditions on set, including delayed pay, spoiled food, bathroom restrictions, and excessive hours, according to extras. At least 14 extras threaten to sue the producers, claiming they were surprised by the film’s topic and felt uncomfortable due to their opposition to Bolsonaro. The São Paulo State Union of Artists and Technicians in Entertainment (Sated-SP) confirmed the complaints and sent delegates to the set.

item.title: Esquerda explora revelação de contato de Flávio com Vorcaro por filme sobre o pai e retoma mote 'bolsomaster' nas redes
item.description: The Brazilian left seized on revelations of contact between Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master to criticize the senator and presidential pre-candidate, accusing him of involvement in a corruption scheme tied to funding a film about his father, Jair Bolsonaro. The messages, leaked by The Intercept and confirmed by O Globo, were used to revive the 'Bolsomaster' narrative, with PT, PSOL, and other lawmakers demanding Federal Police investigations and even preventive detention of Flávio, framing the case as evidence that Bolsonarism and corruption are inherently linked.

item.title: Líder do PL na Câmara sai em defesa de Flávio Bolsonaro: ‘patrocínio privado’
item.description: The leader of the PL in the Chamber, Sóstenes Cavalcante, defended Flávio Bolsonaro after the senator admitted requesting 135 million reais from banker Daniel Vorcaro to finance the film 'Dark Horse', about Jair Bolsonaro's life. The PL leadership stated the sponsorship was entirely private, with no public funds or Rouanet Law involvement, and rejected attempts to politicize the case. Investigations by the STF and reports from The Intercept Brasil suggest possible irregularities in the transfers, including the use of U.S.-based companies linked to Eduardo Bolsonaro.

item.title: Como pré-candidatos de direita à Presidência reagiram ao áudio de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Right-wing presidential pre-candidates reacted to an audio leaked by Intercept Brasil in which Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) sought financial support from banker Daniel Vorcaro to fund a film about Jair Bolsonaro. Romeu Zema (Novo) called the audio a 'slap in the face of decent Brazilians', Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) demanded transparency in public-private relations, and Renan Santos (Missão) accused Flávio of corruption, calling for his arrest and removal from office.

item.title: Leia a íntegra da MP que cria subsídios para gasolina e diesel
item.description: The Lula government announced subsidies for gasoline and diesel in response to fuel price increases caused by the Iran war. The measure, estimated to cost R$ 2.9 billion monthly, includes a subsidy of R$ 0.40 to R$ 0.45 per liter for gasoline and a monthly fiscal impact of R$ 1.7 billion for diesel. The Provisional Measure is available in PDF format.

item.title: Deputados pedem investigação sobre relação entre Vorcaro e Flávio
item.description: Federal deputies from PT, PSOL and PCdoB announced a complaint to the Federal Police, a request to the Federal Revenue Service, and a proposal for a parliamentary inquiry commission to investigate alleged negotiations between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro to finance a film about the Bolsonaro family, involving approximately R$134 million. Leaked messages show Flávio demanding payments, with part of the funds transferred between February and May 2025 to a U.S.-based fund linked to the lawyer of Eduardo Bolsonaro.

item.title: Oposição acusa PT de “criminalização política” e pede CPI do Banco Master
item.description: The opposition leadership in the Chamber of Deputies accused the PT of 'political criminalization' following the leak of audios involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro. The bloc defended the senator and called for a CPI to investigate Banco Master, claiming political motivations behind investigations targeting right-wing figures.

item.title: Áudio de Flávio terá impacto direto em candidatura, diz Erika Hilton
item.description: Deputy Erika Hilton (Psol-SP) stated that the leaked audio of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), in which he asks banker Daniel Vorcaro for money to produce the film Dark Horse, will directly impact his 2026 presidential campaign. She called the case an 'absurd corruption scandal' and suggested it reflects a broader pattern of illicit behavior by the Bolsonaro family. Flávio denies using public funds, saying the request was for private sponsorship only, and reaffirmed his support for a parliamentary inquiry into Banco Master.

item.title: Ouça Flávio pedindo dinheiro a Vorcaro para filme de Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) negotiated with Daniel Vorcaro, founder of Banco Master, to finance the film “Dark Horse,” about Jair Bolsonaro’s trajectory, requesting $24 million in 2025, of which only $10.6 million was disbursed. He confirmed the authenticity of an audio in which he pressed for overdue payments, warning of negative consequences if payments were not made, including damaging the reputation of internationally renowned actors and directors. The funds were channeled through entities linked to the Grupo Entre, including the Havengate Development Fund LP in Texas, whose legal representative is associated with Eduardo Bolsonaro.
